source_title: Lebanese couple in tears as buyer vows not to demolish their A$960,000 home
source_excerpt: A Melbourne couple who spent more than four decades building a family life in their home experienced an emotional farewell when the property was sold at auction for A$960,000. The four-bedroom house in Maidstone, in Melbourne's west, had been their family home since they arrived in Australia from Lebanon in 1982. Although the sale marked the end of their time there, the buyers' decision to retain the existing house rather than demolish it brought them to tears. According to a report published by realestate.com.au on October 30, 2026, the winning buyers made the promise after the auction, giving the longtime owners reassurance that the home would continue to stand.A Melbourne home that held four decades of family memoriesThe property at 26 Marsh Street, Maidstone, became an important part of the couple's life after they settled in Australia. Nelson Alexander auctioneer Ryan Currie told realestate.com.au that the couple had arrived from Lebanon in 1982 and subsequently raised four children in the house. More than 40 years of family life had taken place within its walls, making the property much more than a residential asset for its owners.Two of the couple's four children attended the auction as their parents prepared to leave the home. After spending decades there, the sellers were planning to downsize to a low-maintenance property in Taylors Lakes. The move would bring a change in their living arrangements, but the emotional connection to the Maidstone house remained strong. The property sits on a 586-square-metre block and attracted attention during the sales campaign because of its north-facing orientation and potential for redevelopment. According to Currie, several developers inspected the site, although none attended the auction.The A$960,000 auction and the buyers' decisionThe four-bedroom house was sold on Saturday, October 24, 2026, for A$960,000. The final price was A$50,000 above its published reserve of A$910,000. The auction attracted interest from buyers with different plans for the property. A local family hoping to demolish the existing house and rebuild finished as the underbidder. However, the successful purchasers had a different intention. They wanted to live in the existing home and planned to retain it rather than knock it down.That decision became particularly meaningful to the former owners. After the auction, the couple were eager to meet the winning buyers. When the purchasers told them they intended to keep the house, the conversation prompted an emotional response. Currie recalled that both the husband and wife burst into tears after hearing the news. Their reaction reflected the importance of knowing that the home where they had raised their children would not immediately be demolished following the sale.Why the promise mattered to the sellersFor homeowners, selling a property can involve more than agreeing on a price. A house that has been occupied for decades can hold memories of family milestones, everyday routines and the experience of raising children. In this case, the couple had lived in the Maidstone property for more than four decades, making the prospect of its demolition especially difficult. The buyers' intention to preserve the existing house offered a degree of reassurance during an otherwise significant transition. While the couple would no longer live there, the building itself would remain part of the neighbourhood and continue to serve as a family home.The sale also demonstrated how buyers can approach the same property with different priorities. The underbidding family saw an opportunity to demolish and rebuild, while the successful purchasers preferred to retain the existing residence. The property's redevelopment potential had attracted interest from developers during the campaign, but the eventual outcome was shaped by buyers who wanted to occupy the house as it stood.A new chapter for the Maidstone propertyCurrie said moments like the sellers' emotional reaction made his work rewarding, particularly after a challenging period for Melbourne's property market. The auction was not simply the completion of a transaction for the couple. It marked the end of a long chapter that began when they arrived in Australia and established their family home.The former owners are now preparing for a smaller, low-maintenance home in Taylors Lakes, while the successful buyers intend to make the Maidstone house their family residence. The A$960,000 sale therefore brought a change of ownership without the immediate demolition the sellers had feared. For a couple who raised four children in the house after moving from Lebanon in 1982, the buyers' promise offered an emotional parting gift.
